·5··Public Utility Commission of Texas will come to order to

·6··consider matters that have been dually posted with the

·7··Secretary of State for August 28th, 2026.

·8·· · · · · · · ·Good morning, everyone.

·9·· · · · · · · ·Commissioners, I'm going to propose we

10··take things up in order today.··We'll hear public

11··comment first on items that are not contested cases,

12··then we can take up Items 2 and 3 together and then

14··Item No. 4, if that works for everybody.

17··Patrick, we've been thinking about you and your family,

18··your wife, Leslie.··You've been in our prayers and we're

19··glad that she's doing well enough that you were able to

20··make it back here today.··So, you know, continued

21··progress for her and continue to let us know what you

·3··comment on matters that are within the Commission's

·4··jurisdiction except for pending contested matters.··In

·5··the interest of time, speakers will be limited to three

·6··minutes.

·8··up to speak, Judge Brandon Huckabee.

·9·· · · · · · · ·CHAIRMAN GLEESON:··Good morning, Judge

10··Huckabee.··Nice to see you again.

11·· · · · · · · ·JUDGE HUCKABEE:··Good morning.··Good to see

12··you, as well.

13·· · · · · · · ·Chairman, Commissioners, Brandon Huckabee,

14··Erath County Judge.··You've heard from me before.

15··You've heard -- you've heard from landowners, you've

16··hopefully read thousands of pages of testimony and

17··evidence, so, today, if this is the day you make a

18··decision, I want to talk about something pretty simple;

19··it's called trust.··Because somewhere along the way in

20··this process a lot of people that I represent lost trust

21··that their voices actually matter.

22·· · · · · · · ·These are great people.··They're not

23··activists.··Most of them never imagined they would know

24··what a CCN is, hire an attorney to protect their family

25··property or learn how to be an attorney, or drive to

                   KENNEDY REPORTING SERVICE, INC.
               512.474-2233 order@kennedyreporting.com
                                                                8

·1··Austin hoping someone in state government would listen,

·2··but they did.··They followed the rules, they

·3··participated, they spent their own money, they

·4··rearranged their lives, and many of them are sitting out

·5··here and back at home walking away believing the deck is

·6··stacked against them from the very beginning.··I don't

·7··think we should feel comfortable with that.

·8·· · · · · · · ·They see multibillion dollar corporations

·9··with lawyers and experts, limitless resources, they look

10··towards Austin and see a regulatory system that's

11··complicated, expensive, nearly impossible for an

12··ordinary landowner to navigate and standing in the

13··middle of all of that is a family just trying to protect

14··the place they call home.

15·· · · · · · · ·Commissioners, again, I don't question the

16··need.··Texas needs more power, but surely we can meet

17··that need without making Texans believe their government

18··simply is something else they have to defend their

19··property from, because this isn't just about what line

20··gets selected on a map.··Whichever line is selected

21··becomes someone's reality.··It's somebody's home,

22··somebody's school, somebody's family land, somebody's

23··livelihood, and long after this docket is closed they

24··will live with that decision made in this room.

25·· · · · · · · ·You've heard serious concerns about this

                KENNEDY REPORTING SERVICE, INC.
            512.474-2233 order@kennedyreporting.com
                                                                 9

·1··process, about notice, participation, property rights

·2··and whether affected landowners truly received the

·3··opportunity they deserve.··You now have to decide

·4··whether that process was good enough.··I don't believe

·5··it was, and neither do many of the people that I

·6··represent.··Texas law gives you the authority to approve

·7··and to deny.··I'm asking you to deny.··Not because we

·8··oppose progress, not because we don't understand the

·9··need for reliable electricity, but because getting the

10··electricity where it needs to go cannot be the only

11··measure of whether we got this right.··How we treat

12··Texans along the way matters, too.

13·· · · · · · · ·The people of Erath County aren't asking

14··for special treatment; they're asking for something

15··fundamental.··To know that when an ordinary Texan stands

16··up powerful interests and says this process isn't right

17··your government will actually listen.··Today you have an

18··opportunity to show them it will.

19·· · · · · · · ·Don't pick a route through a flawed process

20··and call it finished.··Deny these lines, show Texans

21··that we can build big things, solve big problems, meet

22··the demands of the future without running over the very

23··people who built this state in the first place.··Thank

24··you.

25·· · · · · · · ·CHAIRMAN GLEESON:··Thank you.

                KENNEDY REPORTING SERVICE, INC.
            512.474-2233 order@kennedyreporting.com
                                                                10

·1·· · · · · · · ·MR. SCHEIFLER:··Judge John Paul Schuster.

·2·· · · · · · · ·JUDGE SCHUSTER:··Good morning.··How are

·3··y'all?··Ready to go?··Morning, Commission, everybody.

·4··My name's John Paul Schuster, I'm the Kinney County

·5··Judge.··My wife and I live on her family ranch there in

·6··Kinney County.··We've been fortunate enough to raise our

·7··three kids there.··I'm also the chairman of our Texas

·8··Border Sub-Regional Planning Commission, which is

·9··created under Chapter 391 of Texas Local Government

10··Code.

11·· · · · · · · ·Our commission adopted a policy opposing

12··the Howard lease line and all the other lines, but

13··mainly that one through our Kinney and Uvalde counties

14··who serve on our 391, obviously to protect private

15··property, natural resources, public health, local

16··economies, and so much more.

17·· · · · · · · ·We're very fortunate.··On July 30th our

18··commission sat down face to face with AEP and CPS.··They

19··came to us and sat down with us, and I commend those

20··folks for that.··We brought up many concerns, many

21··concerns you've already heard throughout this process,

22··throughout these lines, throughout Texas.··These issues

23··must be considered and resolved through environmental

24··assessments before any condemnation construction of any

25··of the projects, Howard lease line, whatever it may be,

                KENNEDY REPORTING SERVICE, INC.
            512.474-2233 order@kennedyreporting.com
                                                                11

·1··through our jurisdictions, boots on the ground seeing

·2··what's there, not from satellites.··Due diligence.

·3·· · · · · · · ·To many the answers came down to

·4··engineering would be there and they would all happen

·5··after the route's approved.··That's backwards, that's

·6··too late.··The next generation, the damage is done.··The

·7··next great Texans will suffer if we don't do this right

·8··the first time.

·9·· · · · · · · ·For decades we've had to live with illegal

10··immigration, border crime and so forth like that.

11··Building this transmission line this size through our

12··part of the country is a superhighway, not only into our

13··counties, but into Texas and in the United States.··And

14··you know how the last six year have been; it hasn't been

15··fun for us.

16·· · · · · · · ·Several property owners were not affected

17··by the preliminary link shown at the open houses nor did

18··they receive information.··Links were added later and

19··those landowners learned their property was on the path

20··after formal notice.··Limited resources, limited time,

21··just weeks that they had to try to understand the scope

22··and size of this project, find counsel if they were able

23··to, and file as intervenors; a common theme across the

24··state with these projects, as you well know.··Our ranch

25··had two blue lines and it disappeared.··We were one of

                KENNEDY REPORTING SERVICE, INC.
            512.474-2233 order@kennedyreporting.com
                                                                12

·1··the fortunate ones, but we may still get another one.

·2·· · · · · · · ·The applicants had months, teams of

·3··lawyers, engineers and consultants.··We did not.··Just

·4··checking legal boxes is not the same as giving people

·5··meaningful opportunity to participate, due diligence.··I

·6··asked AEP and CPS, as residents in the counties that we

·7··serve and live we, too, have shareholders; our kids, our

·8··grandkids, the next generation of Texan.

·9·· · · · · · · ·The right-of-way does not just take a strip

10··of land; it strips us of future use.··It also lowers our

11··land values and changes what we have to hand down to the

12··next generation.··On July 30th ERCOT told us that,

13··hey -- the AEP ERCOT said, hey, equivalent, yes, and now

14··Governor Abbot said we need to audit this, we need to

15··slow this down.··That batch process was just a

16··preliminary.

17·· · · · · · · ·We won't know until December the 10th.

18··December the 10th.··If load assumptions are supported

19··and verified then, yeah, let's work on it then.··Get it

20··back to the legislation and let them have the

21··understanding clearly of what should have been done and

22··what should have been proposed.··Due diligence.··Time is

23··our friend and if you continue to accelerate the process

24··it would crush the people with the least amount of time

25··and fewest resources.

                KENNEDY REPORTING SERVICE, INC.
            512.474-2233 order@kennedyreporting.com
                                                                13

·1·· · · · · · · ·I ask you to pump the brakes, deny the

·2··applications as presented, review what December the 10th

·3··says, and ask those folks to go back to the drawing

·4··board and come back to our communities with better

·5··answers, better choices and better information.··Simply

·6··stated, due diligence from all.··Don't make a decision

·7··today and make us have permanent decisions based on

·8··assumptions today.··Thank you and God bless.

·9·· · · · · · · ·CHAIRMAN GLEESON:··Thank you.

10·· · · · · · · ·MR. SCHEIFLER:··Next, Todd Staples.

11·· · · · · · · ·CHAIRMAN GLEESON:··Good morning.

12·· · · · · · · ·MR. STAPLES:··Good morning, Mr. Chairman,

13··Commissioners.··I'm Todd Staples, President of the Texas

14··Oil and Gas Association.··Thank you for your leadership

15··for Texas and the chance to testify today.

16·· · · · · · · ·I want to begin by stating a fact that is

17··within your power to reverse.··The fact is, America's

18··most important energy security region is at risk.··West

19··Texas operations, West Texas homes, schools, businesses

20··are all threatened today because it lacks access to

21··dependable, reliable, affordable interconnection into

22··the ERCOT grid.··This is not hypothetical or conceptual.

23··It is real, it is tangible, it's immediate.

24·· · · · · · · ·Last week during this hearing that you were

25··conducting at the same time ERCOT was meeting with us

                KENNEDY REPORTING SERVICE, INC.
            512.474-2233 order@kennedyreporting.com
                                                                14

·1··and our operators who are responsible for delivering 90

·2··percent of the state's oil and gas that Texans depend

·3··upon every day, and what they were discussing is how to

·4··manage imminent rolling blackouts in the Permian.··The

·5··lack of dispatchable generation and transmission in West

·6··Texas is a topic that ERCOT, the PUC, and consumers have

·7··been working to solve for over a dozen years.··Our

·8··state's best engineers and managers have conclusively

·9··confirmed the Permian plan is the most expedient and

10··cost effective solution.

11·· · · · · · · ·We're not talking about an issue that would

12··be nice to address or convenient to address.··This need

13··is about the operate the basics of modern life.··No

14··Texan should be denied access to the basics:··water,

15··transportation, communications and power.··Power is what

16··makes it all work.··There are six gigawatts of unmet,

17··unconnected low demand in West Texas now.··We're not

18··thinking about data centers in the future.··These are

19··immediate needs; it's today, not tomorrow.··And,

20··thankfully, the PUC and ERCOT have been working on plans

21··to address this failure since 2019 through a process

22··that has been all available to the public.

23·· · · · · · · ·Let me reemphasize the urgency that we

24··face.··We aren't discussing the curtailment of splash

25··pads and swimming pools.··We're facing curtailing

                KENNEDY REPORTING SERVICE, INC.
            512.474-2233 order@kennedyreporting.com
                                                                15

·1··critical infrastructure.··Reliability is what will keep

·2··us safe during the next winter storm and, if West Texas

·3··cannot be reliable, the rest of Texas has no chance for

·4··security.··Establishing right-of-ways for infrastructure

·5··projects is one of the most difficult challenges facing

·6··any local or state government.··There's not a road, a

·7··waterline, a power line, communications or pipeline

·8··built that did not have to address these challenges.

·9·· · · · · · · ·I have every confidence you as the PUC can

10··and will do everything possible to mitigate impacts to

11··landowners, and we applaud you for seeking to find the

12··most reasonable routes and to ensure that those impacted

13··in this process receive full and just compensation.··But

14··to delay is to prevent thousands of landowners and

15··Texans from receiving the peace of mind and certainty
